Commentary.Commentary: The target is once again a tricky one. Pakistan managed to defend something similar in the first T20I. Can they chase it down or will new Zealand level the series? Join us in a few minutes to find out.

The duo added a 42-run stand and that too at good pace. The skipper departed but Anderson ensured they crossed the 150-run mark. A mixed bowling effort by Pakistan. Hasan Ali and Faheem Ashraf had a day to forget at the office but the spinners once again managed to dry the runs out. However, it was Shaheen Afridi who was the pick as he finished with a three-fer and only gave away 20 in his 4.

New Zealand have finished with a total which one would say is a very competitive one. It was almost a similar story to the last T20I, this time though they finished well at the end. Munro got them off to the ideal start as he went bonkers in the Powerplay. New Zealand were 50 for 1 after the first six but then the downfall started. They lost Munro and de Grandhomme in quick succession. Taylor too was run out for not a lot but then Williamson and Anderson came to the rescue.
Another length ball around middle, Anderson pulls it through mid-wicket for another couple. So a good last over for New Zealand and the finish with 153!
He will also face the last ball as this is flicked towards deep square leg for a couple. 150 up.
Adam Milne is the new man in.

OUT! RUN OUT! Southee siwngs and misses. Anderson wants strike so he goes for the run. Sarfraz throws it towards the bowler. Southee does try to come in between but the ball misses him. Afridi collects the ball and hits bull's eye at his end. Anderson will be on strike though.
This is hit down to long on for a run. Anderson is off strike now.
Tim Southee walks out.
OUT! Seifert holes out! The slower ball on middle, Tim is very early into the shot. He only hits it high up in the air towards long on. Shadab Khan settles under it and takes it with ease.
SIX! With such shots, the can cross 160. Plays the paddle and is helped with a full toss. Seifert lofts it over the keeper for a biggie. Ideal start to the last over.

NOT OUT! He is safe and due to the dive, he is quite comfortably in. Full and around middle, Anderson hits it down to long on. They run the first one hard and go for the second. The fielder there throws it towards the bowler's end. He collects the ball and dislodges the stumps. An appeal and the umpire takes it upstairs. Replays show the batsman is safe. So not 20 from the over but 16 from it. A very good one and now they can go over 150.
Another run out appeal. Seifert this time though feels he is safe.
Another couple! Full and on the pads, CA flicks it fine towards backward square leg for a couple.

SIX! FLAT! The slower one and Corey was waiting for it. He thwacks it over the mid-wicket fence. The fielder did look interested for a while but he had no chance. 12 from the first 4. Can they make it a 20 run over?
The batter there tried to paddle but was way too early into the shot. It goes off the toe end towards deep mid-wicket. A run.

FOUR! Hasan Ali has not had a good day today. Seifert walks down the track and hits it through covers. He takes it on the full and hence times it wonderfully away from the sweeper. They need a big over here.
A single to begin the penultimate over. Anderson strokes it down to long on.

Yes, he does and so easily it could have been another wicket. A yorker again on middle, the batter once again jams it out to covers. Corey sets off again but is sent back. Shadab this time tries the underarm throw but does not hit the bull's eye. Anderson did dive to get in. It may have saved him. A brilliant over by Afirid comes to an end. The 18th over just goes for a single.
Another dot, another yorker, it is jammed out. Lovely stuff, only a single and a wicket form this over so far. Can he end it well?
Direct hit needed but Shadab misses. A low full toss on off, Seifert drives it to covers. Corey goes for a run but is sent back. Khan has a shy but misses.
Only a run from the first three ball as this is eased down to long on.
Lovely bowling! Slower ball outside off, Anderson aims to hit it on the leg side but misses.
Tim Seifert is the new man in.

OUT! In the air... caught! Williamson departs and a timely wicket for Pakistan as this partnership was starting to look very dangerous. The slower ball on middle, Kane walks across his stumps and tries to flick. He gets elevation but not the distance. Zaman in the deep square leg region runs to his left and takes a good catch. A good innings by Williamson comes to an end. He held fort at one end when New Zealand kept losing wickets at the other. 150 now though looks a little tough.
Shaheen Afridi is back on.

FOUR! Yes, he can. 6,4,4 to end the over. 16 from this one. 35 from the last three. This one was a fortunate boundary. A yorker on the pads, Anderson tries to flick but the ball takes the inside edge and goes fine down the leg side for a boundary.

FOUR! 10 from the last two deliveries and New Zealand are on a roll here. Short and it is the slower one. Anderson pulls it in the gap at the mid-wicket region. Boundary. Can he end the over with a bang now?
SIX! Brute, powerful, call that what you want. A low full toss outside off, not a very bad delivery. Anderson gets under it and tonks it over long on for a biggie.
A dot to follow up two singles. Slower ball outside off, Anderson is way too early into the shot and is beaten.
Slower ball outside off, Williamson guides it towards point. He is right at the edge of the circle and a run is taken.
Full and straight, Anderson hits it down to long on for a run.
Hasan Ali is back on.
Single to end Shadab's spell. 4-0-24-0 is what it reads. Another decent night for him. Flatter and outside off, Corey slaps it down to long off for a run.
Toe-end! The ball never arrived there. Short and slow, Williamson is way too early into the pull. It goes off the lower portion of the bat towards long on for a run.
Hits this away from the bowler and down towards mid on for a single.
Has the courage to toss it up again. Anderson smashes it back to the bowler who fields it well.
Flatter and quicker on middle, Williamson is hurried into the shot and mistimes it towards mid-wicket. Only a run.
FOUR! Dealing in boundaries is New Zealand now. Shadad gives it air around off, Williamson lofts it over covers and the ball races away to the fence.
Shadab Khan is back on.

FOUR! Off the inner half but New Zealand won't care. 11 from the over. Full and on middle, Corey swings but the ball goes off the inner half between the gap he got a boundary few balls ago. This time though, the player at deep mid-wicket is late to go after it and then he had no chance.
Excellent comeback! A yorker outside off, Anderson tries to whip it but gets a bottom edge to the keeper.

FOUR! Slower ball and it has been picked early. Anderson pulls it in between deep square leg and deep mid-wicket. A boundary results. Need to keep going if they are to reach the 150-run mark. Also this is only the second boundary in the last 10 overs.
Not a lot Corey could have done with this delivery. A yorker on middle, it is jammed out.
A yorker outside off, Kane guides it down to third man for a run. Not a lot he could have done with that ball.

Another mix-up! What is up with the Kiwi batters today? Williamson plays a good paddle scoop over the short fine leg fielder. Afridi there hares after the ball, then dives and pushes it back in. The batsmen run two and Kane wants the third. He sets off but in time is sent back. The fielder fires it to the keeper but KW makes it in.
Faheem Ashraf is back on.
Williamson has probably decided to step on the gas, however, he is not timing it. Goes for the heave but mistimes it towards deep mid-wicket. Another single taken.
Full and on the pads, Anderson flicks it through square leg for a single.
Kane makes room and then cuts it through point for a run.
Goes fuller this time on middle, Anderson eases it down to long on for another single.
Good length on middle, the batsman blocks it out.
Slower and shorter on middle, Williamson pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Shaheen Afridi is back on.
The googly on middle, kept out. 9 runs but a wicket from it, that too a big one.
WIDE! Down the leg side and it has been wided.
Slightly shorter on middle, it is pulled through square leg for a run.
Corey Anderson is the new man in.

OUT! Taylor is well short. Not sure why that was taken upstairs as Taylor himself was walking. This is last thing New Zealand wanted. They would have hoped for this pair to bat deep but it is not to be. A needless run. Williamson flicks it through mid-wicket. They run the first one hard and then go for a second. Asif Ali there is quick to the ball and he fires it to the bowler. It is right besides the stumps and Shadab collects it and whips the bails off. The players appeal, the umpire goes up to check and replays show, Taylor is well short. Ross fails to make an impact this time and Pakistan continue to dominate.
Run out! Taylor has started to walk back but the umpire, just to be sure has taken is upstairs.

FOUR! Much, much-needed! A top shot also. Shadab gives it air around off, Williamson gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over covers for a boundary. The skipper holds the key here, needs to play till the end.
Flatter outside off, Taylor cuts it through point for another run. New Zealand have to be content with singles at the moment.
On the shorter side outside off, Williamson slaps it through covers for a single.
Two dots to end as Taylor plays this ball really late towards point. The runs once again have dried up after the Powerplay.
Uses his feet again and pushes it towards covers.
Flatter again on off, Williamson punches it through covers and takes a run.

Confusion again! Taylor once again dances down the track, he misses the flick this time. The ball hits his pads and rolls towards the off side. Taylor wants a run, Williamson is hesitant but then goes for it. They complete it with ease in the end. Leg bye signaled.
Fires this one on off, Williamson goes back and guides it through point for a single.
Taylor uses his feet and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Good running! This is tossed up on middle, Williamson works it through mid-wicket. They run the first one hard which enables them to take another. 4 from Shadab's over, another tight one.
Again tosses this one up, the ball turns slightly. Taylor gets an outside edge through covers for a run.
Brings the sweep shot out and connects well but only for a run towards deep square leg.
Three dots! Flatter around off, Williamson guides it towards point.
Kane lunges and strokes it to covers. Two dots to begin with.
Tosses it up around middle, Williamson keeps it out off the front foot.
Around off, solidly defended. 3 runs and a wicket from the over. 18/2 since the Powerplay.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Ross Taylor walks in at number 5, replacing de Grandhomme.

OUT! Caught! Well, Colin tries for a grand hit but is back in the hut instead. Tossed up very slowly outside off, de Grandhomme jumps out of his crease and looks to go big but is not quite to the pitch of the ball. Mistimes it high in the air and Shoaib Malik takes it quite easily at long on.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Drives this straight back but Wasim fumbles and deflects the ball to long off. Hits himself with his hand on his head. An easy single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Slightly shorter than full, Kane punches it towards long off but Shadab dives to his left and makes a clean stop.
Another long hop, pulled through mid-wicket for a couple.
Dropped very short, outside off, spinning away, Williamson waits and waits and waits for it but the ball never arrives. Eventually he plays the cut and gets a bottom edge back to the bowler.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Short and outside off, turning away, de Grandhomme looks to cut but misses.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Shadab Khan to bowl now.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, pushed towards long off for one.
Tossed up outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Short and outside off, Williamson punches it through the covers where the fielder dives over the ball and allows it through. Two runs taken and skipper Sarfraz is not happy.
Colin de Grandhomme walks in at number 4, replacing Munro. Imad Wasim is back on, after going for 13 in his opener.

OUT! STUMPED! Unfortunate way to go for Munro. He jumps down the track, looks to swing hard but the ball takes the inside edge and hits him on the boot. Now, normally, the ball should be deflecting to the leg side but instead it rolls back. Easy stumping for Sarfraz. Munro is yards out. Misses out on a half century but Pakistan have a big opening.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a run.
Comes down the track and flicks it over mid-wicket for a couple.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.

LBW APPEAL, turned down, but hang on, HAVE PAKISTAN MISSED A RUN OUT? The arm ball, around leg, sliding down, Munro backs away, looking to punch but misses and is hit on the pads. The bowler and keeper appeal and meanwhile, Williamson calls Munro through for a single. Sarfraz hares to his left as the ball is near point, tries to pick up and throw but does not collect it cleanly. Munro was not even halfway through.
Mohammad Hafeez is back on.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler. 3 runs and a wicket from the over. 50/1 in the Powerplay.
Kane Williamson, the captain, walks in at number 3, replacing Phillips.

OUT! Caught behind! The opening stand is broken, once again on 50. The 18-year old has done it for his side. A length ball, outside leg, Phillips looks to play this to the leg side but the ball seams away, takes something, either inside edge or the pad, on first look, to the keeper behind. Afridi straightaway appeals while Phillips does not walk. Umpire Shozab Raza initially stands still, then raises his finger, after a nod of his head. No review from Phillips, so must have been an inside edge. Yes. Replays detect only wood.
On middle and leg, swinging in, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
A short ball, punched through mid off for a very quick single. Direct hit at the bowler's end might have been interesting. 50 IS UP, IN JUST 33 BALLS.
Outside off, crunched straight to cover.
That tailed back in a long way, Munro managed to flick it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Shaheen Afridi introduced.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on for one. 10 from that over.
FOUR! HAMMERED! A short ball outside off, Munro punches it through the covers, a tad uppishly, but it is in the gap!
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and outside off, blasted through the covers for a single.
Gets away with this one as well. Just a run towards mid on.
ANOTHER FREE HIT. What can we expect now?
THAT IS A NO BALL TOO! The Free Hit does not count for much, even though it a full toss, but the next delivery might. Driven through the covers for a single.
FREE HIT TIME.
NO BALL! Hasan has overstepped and bowled a length ball on middle, pushed towards mid off.
Full and straight, pushed towards mid off.
Fourth bowler in 5 overs. Hasan Ali onto bowl now.
Pushes this towards mid on.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off this time.
On middle, pushed towards mid on.

PUT DOWN! The Professor is at fault now. A length ball, on middle and leg, Munro heaves this high in the air. Does not get enough distance and Hafeez is in with a chance at long on. He comes running in, dives and takes the catch but while landing on the dive, his elbow hits the ground very hard and the ball pops out. A single taken. Big miss.
SIX! Wow. Really, wow. A short ball outside off, extra bounce but what does Munro do? He leaps and plays a tennis-like forehand smash over long off!
A slower ball, short in lenth, outside off, a pull attempted is missed.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Easy cricket. Stand and deliver. A length ball outside off, Munro backs away and clobbers it over mid off for a boundary!
Same shot, this time the fielder stops the ball while the batsmen have no communication issues. Easy single taken.

RUN OUT CHANCE, MISSED! Shadab Khan, of all the people. A short ball, Phillips punches it towards mid on and sets off for a single. But Munro at the other end is ball-watching and Glenn has to return, from the halfway mark. Shadab is in with a chance to run the batsman out but he misfields and does not collect the ball at all. Phillips makes it back easily.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
BEATEN! How did that miss the stumps? The flatter delivery to start, Munro backs away to cut but is done in by the pace. He misses and luckily for him, the ball just evades the leg pole!
The Professor is on. Mohammad Hafeez to bowl.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
A slower short ball, outside off, Colin swings early and misses.
FOUR! FETCH THAT! Back-to-back boundaries for Munro! Short and outside off, Munro goes back and punches it through the covers!

FOUR! Seemed like a mishit but in the Middle East, it is not actually necessary to hit out of the middle. A length ball, on middle, Munro looks to slog but the ball hits the higher part of the bat. Clears mid on comfortably.
A touch short around off, moving away, Munro looks to pull but mistimes it towards short mid-wicket.
Faheem Ashraf to bowl from the other end.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single. 13 from the opening over!
Outside off, punched uppishly but wide of the bowler, down the ground for one.
Fuller on middle, pushed through long on for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.

Excellent fielding by Babar Azam. Desperate stuff. A touch short on middle, Colin punches it down the ground. The ball almost makes it to the ropes but Babar gives it a good chase from mid on and at the last moment, dives to pull the ball back in. Three runs taken.
SIX! FEROCIOUS! What a start! Full and around off, Munro gets down on a knee and slogs it wayyyy over mid-wicket!
The players are already onto the field, in the Ring Of Fire. Colin Munro and Glenn Phillips are the openers for New Zealand. As expected, Imad Wasim will start off the proceedings with the ball.

Danny Morrison took an interview of Colin Munro a few minutes ago. The latter admits that this is his favourite format as it allows him to be aggressive right from the word go. Stresses that right balance is the key. Adds that he tries to cover his stumps and then play his shots. On his bowling, he says that he is enjoying his game overall, though sometimes his bowling does not come off. Points out that the job expected out of him with the ball is to stop boundaries. Agrees that he is aspiring to make it to the ODI World Cup squad but it is a very long journey, with the one-day squad doing well currently. Wants to keep performing consistently and then let his fate decide.

A must-win encounter for the Black Caps, no doubt. But they will be fresher than their counterparts. In the last game, they were rusty. Pakistan, on the other hand, are just a win away from their 11th consecutive series victory in T20Is. In terms of matches, they are on a 7-game winning streak. Will that extend tonight? We shall see...

Why try and mend something if it is not broken? The Kiwis seem to be going by that saying. They are unchanged from the previous game. Pakistan, on the other hand, have got a big boost, with Fakhar Zaman recovering from his knee injury and passed fit. He replaces Sahibzada Farhan.

TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. Kane Williamson has called it correctly and boy, NEW ZEALAND ARE BATTING FIRST. Now, now, now... the number 1 T20I team in the world has not been the greatest when it comes to chasing. Or... even while batting. If the Kiwis manage to get to 150, then we could have a really good contest on your hands.

A ripper of a first T20I. New Zealand almost pipping out Pakistan. Satisfied crowds. Now, the carnival moves to Dubai. Pakistan, who are in a busy home season have been travelling to and fro between Abu Dhabi and Dubai so frequently, that it almost seems like Pakistan Super League is in action. Hello and a warm welcome to the second T20I between Pakistan and New Zealand in Dubai.
